editorNote: The second week of December turns the computer counter into a comparison table: Atari movie cartridges, a new premium 5200 system, ColecoVision arcade promises, and Commodore's 64K home-computer pitch all fight for holiday attention.
morningLine: Movie cartridges and 64K home computers define the December 6 holiday counter.

lead.headline: Movie Cartridges Meet the 64K Christmas Pitch
lead.summary: In the week of December 6, 1982, Atari's E.T. and Raiders of the Lost Ark cartridges give the 2600 familiar movie names while the Commodore 64 and Atari 5200 ask shoppers to spend more for memory, graphics, sound, and a longer-lived machine.
lead.confidence: Week-specific retail framing built from verified November 1982 game releases and 1982 hardware launches.

computerItems.label: Game Shelf
computerItems.headline: E.T. Keeps Atari Tied to the Year's Biggest Movie
computerItems.summary: The Atari 2600 E.T. cartridge remains a high-visibility holiday item because the film is still leading domestic theaters into December.
computerItems.confidence: November 1982 cartridge release and December 1982 box-office context verified.

computerItems.label: Adventure Counter
computerItems.headline: Raiders Gives the 2600 a Map-and-Inventory Pitch
computerItems.summary: Raiders of the Lost Ark turns a film license into a more elaborate Atari 2600 adventure, a contrast with the simpler action cartridges beside it.

computerItems.label: Home Computer Desk
computerItems.headline: Commodore 64 Sells Memory as the Simple Number
computerItems.summary: Commodore's 1982 machine lets dealers point to 64K RAM, color graphics, and sound when families ask why a home computer costs more than a console.

computerItems.label: Console Desk
computerItems.headline: Atari 5200 Tries for Premium Shelf Space
computerItems.summary: The 5200 SuperSystem gives Atari a higher-end console story for shoppers who already know the 2600 name.

softwareList.name: VisiCalc
softwareList.detail: Still the spreadsheet name many buyers recognize when a computer is justified for home finance or small business.

softwareList.name: WordStar
softwareList.detail: A familiar word-processing package in office and serious home-computing conversations.

softwareList.name: dBASE II
softwareList.detail: Database software that helps sell micros as office machines rather than only game boxes.

softwareList.name: Microsoft BASIC
softwareList.detail: A common entry point for owners typing programs from manuals and magazines.

softwareList.name: Choplifter!
softwareList.detail: Broderbund's rescue game remains a strong computer-game name for the Apple II shelf.

Premium console positioning for the holiday season.

priceWatch.note: Games such as Choplifter! sit beside practical applications in computer stores.

market.headline: Holiday Buyers Compare Consoles With Computers
market.summary: The week's sales floor is a contest between immediate arcade-style fun and the promise that a home computer can play games, teach BASIC, and handle practical work after Christmas.
market.confidence: Synthesis from verified 1982 product releases and holiday timing.

bbsNote.headline: Modem Note
bbsNote.summary: After store hours, 300-baud callers trade cartridge tips, BASIC snippets, and local board numbers while the mass market still learns what a modem can do.

curiosity.headline: Cinema Lobby
curiosity.summary: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial remains the No. 1 domestic film for the December 10-12, 1982 weekend, reinforcing why Atari wants the name on game shelves.

briefs.headline: E.T. Still Leads Theaters
briefs.summary: Box Office Mojo lists E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial at No. 1 for the December 10-12 domestic weekend.

briefs.headline: Tootsie Opens Strong
briefs.summary: Tootsie appears among the top domestic films for the December 10-12 weekend, adding a new adult-comedy hit to the holiday movie conversation.

briefs.headline: Hall & Oates Take the Singles Lead
briefs.summary: The Billboard Hot 100 dated December 11, 1982 puts Maneater by Daryl Hall & John Oates at No. 1.

briefs.headline: Zaxxon Keeps the Isometric Look Fresh
briefs.summary: Sega's Zaxxon remains a recognizable 1982 arcade name for stores and magazines discussing arcade-style computer entertainment.

periodAd.headline: Holiday Special: Movie Games and 64K Machines
periodAd.summary: Ask for Atari E.T. and Raiders cartridges, Atari 5200 demonstrations, ColecoVision arcade favorites, and Commodore 64 holiday bundles at your local computer counter.
periodAd.confidence: Composite period-style advertisement based on verified products.

classifieds.headline: BASIC tutoring
classifieds.copy: Evening lessons for new home-computer owners. Bring your manual and cassette recorder.

classifieds.headline: Cartridge swap
classifieds.copy: 2600 owners meet Saturday to trade duplicates before Christmas.

worldFallback.headline: Editors Hold the Front to Games
worldFallback.summary: No routine world or sports item displaces this week's console, software, and culture story.
